en:
Just the two of us...
And with someone I only met a little while ago.
I know it's already very late.
We're walking down this dark hallway with only the moonlight to see by.{p}
Should I just keep following him?{p}

For a while now, the only sound has been two sets of footsteps.
There's no one here but him and me.
How did it come to this?
How...{p}

Whenever someone finished their story, that person disappeared.
Each time a story ended, they vanished, one after another.
And now there are just the two of us.
I came to the old school building just as he told me to.{p}
...His footsteps stopped.{p}

"This is the classroom.
Come on, go in.
...Come to think of it, I haven't introduced myself yet.
My name is Tomoharu Hosoda.
I'm a second-year.
...Now, let's begin the last story."{p}

And so we went into a classroom.
...So at last, it's come down to just you and me.
{a}.
Listen carefully to the story I'm about to tell you.
The story I'm going to tell is very much like what's happening to us right now.
That's why I came here.
This is fate.
Fate is guiding us.
Are you ready?
...All right, I'm going to begin.{p}

Nice to meet you.
My name is Tomoharu Hosoda.
I'm a second-year.
...So the seventh person never showed up after all.
It looks like my story will be the last one, so why don't we move somewhere else to set the mood a little?
We've waited this long and they haven't come, so I doubt the seventh person is coming now.
I think it'll be fine if we leave here.
Come on, everyone.
Please follow me.{p}

...This gathering was planned to mark the old school building being torn down, right?
So I thought we'd tell the story in the old school building.
We might as well, right?
It's off-limits now, but if we sneak in quietly, nobody will know.
Besides, the story I'm going to tell is about this old school building.{p}

...It's dark, isn't it?
There's no electricity, so it can't be helped.
Please watch your step.
The floor's pretty rotten.
It makes a nasty sound when you step on it.
Creak, creak, creak, creak... It's like a grudge weeping.{p}

...Here we are.
This is the classroom.
Go on in, everyone.
Come inside and sit wherever you like.
Well then, everyone, shall we begin?{p}

{a}{f:|}, do you know the restroom ghost story connected with this old school building?
There are a lot of famous restroom ghost stories, aren't there?
"Give me some paper..."
There's the one about the pale hand that comes up out of the toilet bowl saying that.
The one about two glaring red eyes peering up out of a pit toilet.
...There are all sorts, right?
But the most famous one has got to be Hanako-san.
You knock on the door, and from inside a stall that should be empty comes Hanako-san's voice. And then, when you open the door, there stands Hanako-san...
The Hanako-san story has spread all over the country, under different names and in different forms.
The ghost's gender varies, and so does its name.
In some versions, people know what the ghost really is and why it appears; others are shrouded in mystery.{p}

The one thing they all have in common is that they appear in restrooms.
That's how the strange spirits that appear in restrooms came to be called Hanako-san.
And naturally, this school has its own Hanako-san rumor too.
So what I'm proposing is that we try an experiment to summon that Hanako-san ourselves.{p}

...What do you say, {a}{f:|}?
Won't you give it a try?
I'll do it
No way
That's the spirit.{p}

I just knew you'd say that.
Well then, before we go to the restroom where Hanako-san is actually said to appear, listen to my story for a bit.{p}

This happened decades ago...
So there's no way to check whether it's true.
It might really have happened, or maybe it's just made up.
Well, we'll be able to see for ourselves soon enough.
The whole thing started in this very classroom.
It was right around this time of year.
One muggy summer day.
Back then, students who had failed their final exams were being kept after school.
They were made to work through make-up class worksheets.{p}How about you, {a}{f:|}?{p}You've failed a test before, haven't you?
Yes, I have
No, I haven't
I don't really remember

...That was the mistake.
The teacher who was asked agreed without giving it a thought.
And then that teacher went home, forgetting all about those six.
For some reason, the janitor making the rounds that night didn't notice them either.
I heard this later, but the janitor insisted they had checked, and that nobody was there at the time.
Either the janitor was lying, or some power was at work that made them invisible for just an instant...
Anyway, those six were forgotten by everyone and left behind in this classroom.{p}

By the way, {a}{f:|}.
You haven't gone to the restroom even once this whole time. Are you okay?{p}{f:By any chance|Um...}, you don't need to go to the restroom or anything{f:?|, do you?}
Yes, I do
No, I don't

I see.
Sorry for asking you that, but you'd better hold it a little longer.
At least until my story is over.
Otherwise, something bad will happen.{p}So just hold it a little longer, okay?
I can't hold it. I'm going to the restroom.
I'll hold it like you said

Anyway, as for the six left behind for make-up class, the teacher in charge never came to check on them, and they gradually got uneasy.
But this was the make-up class for an important final exam, so they couldn't afford to fail it.
All six of them had their own reasons.
If they failed it, they'd be barred from club activities, or their parents would get called in, that kind of thing.
So they couldn't just go home.{p}

When they happened to look at the clock, it was already past nine.
But I think that in itself is strange.
Why didn't they notice until nine?
However hard they were concentrating on their make-up work, these were the kind of people who end up in make-up class in the first place. Could they really stay focused that long?{p}Don't you think it's abnormal not to notice until after nine?
I think it's abnormal
Not really
Right?{p}

Someone should have suggested going home right then.
But no one said it.
They thought it was odd, but they kept on with their make-up work by the light of the dim fluorescent lamps.
Even so, could a few make-up worksheets really take that long?
After all, the make-up class is for people who failed.
I've taken it plenty of times myself, so I know: even with my bad grades, I don't find it all that hard.
That's the level we're talking about.
Or maybe it was harder back then?{p}

It was when the clock passed ten.
One of them finally ran out of patience.
"Hey.
You think they forgot about us?"
It was the one question nobody wanted asked.
And the other five looked at one another.
"No way.
I can't imagine the teacher would just abandon us."
One of them blurted out an answer like that.
The one who said it wasn't sure either, but didn't want to believe they'd been abandoned, so that was the answer that came out.
I know just how that feels.
"Then why hasn't the teacher come, this late?
It's already past ten, man."{p}

Then he pointed at the clock hanging on the classroom wall.
"Never mind that, have you all finished the make-up work?
If you're done, we can just go get the teacher ourselves."
One of the girls said it firmly, as if to drive away her unease.
"...I guess you've got a point."{p}

And so they all went back to their make-up work.
But still, the make-up work didn't end.
Every problem gave them the illusion that they were being made to do the same part over and over.
It shouldn't have been that hard, yet somehow it never ended.
It felt like being made to work through a problem book that would never end, no matter how many problems they solved.{p}

When they looked at the clock, it was still only 10:20.
More time should have passed by then, but hardly any had.{p}
Then, after a while...{p}

The clock still read 10:20.
"...Hey, isn't that clock stopped?"
The other girl murmured it, sounding helpless.
It was a fear they had all already sensed.{p}

Can't you see it in the dark?
What time do you think that clock says right now?
It says 10:20.
Ever since that day, the hands of that clock have stayed at 10:20, all this time.{p}Well?
Do you want to examine that clock?
I'll examine it
I won't examine it
...Go on, get closer.{p}

You see it?
It's just an ordinary clock, nothing special about it.
It's pretty dusty, though.
Let's open it up.{p}

...There's no battery in it anymore.
That's why it doesn't run.
But you know, this clock is strange.
Say you move the hands, right?
Before you know it, they've gone back to 10:20.{p}

"Whoa!"
The other five all screamed at once.
They looked, and on the wall where the clock had hung, there was a stain like a human face.
For an instant, it looked like a skull.
...But when they looked closely, it was just a stain.
"...Don't scare us like that."{p}

The one who had taken the clock off the wall hurriedly put it back.
More than examining the clock, they wanted that creepy stain hidden.{p}
Just then, one of them suddenly stood up from his seat.{p}

"...Um.
I'm going to the restroom."
He must have been holding it in for a long time.
He was squirming in place.
Of course, nobody stopped him, and they wondered why he'd bother announcing he was going.
But he looked around at everyone's faces, reluctant to go.
That's right.
He was scared to go alone.
The old school building late at night, already deserted and dead silent.
The six of them were the only ones there.
Anyone would be scared to walk to the restroom all alone through an old school building like that.
But nobody went with him.
With no other choice, he decided to go alone.{p}
Down the long, dark hallway, across floorboards that looked ready to give way any second.{p}

The five wrestled with their worksheets, trying to finish the make-up work as fast as they could.
But the stain behind the clock bothered them, and they just couldn't concentrate.
"...Hey. Isn't this enough already?
Even if none of us finished the worksheets, the teacher's not gonna get mad.
Let's go get the teacher."
Finally unable to stand it, one of them brought it up.
No one objected anymore.
"...Let's do that.
When he gets back from the restroom, let's all go to the teacher together."
Everyone nodded at the idea.{p}

But he didn't come back.
They waited and waited, but he never came back.
The clock had stopped, so they couldn't even tell how much time had passed since then.
When fear takes hold of your mind and time passes in silence, it feels very long.
So in reality, maybe only a minute or two had gone by.
An awkward silence passed.{p}

"...I'll go get him."
With that, one of them dashed out of the classroom.{p}

They called after him, but he was already out of the classroom.
And the creaking of footsteps on the hallway floor faded into the distance.
The four who remained looked at one another.
They were all afraid.{p}

An indescribable fear, as though they had strayed into another world.
If they left the old school building and went through the school gate, the usual scenery should have been waiting there.
And yet, for some reason, they had the strange feeling that they couldn't get out of here.
And they could tell just by looking into each other's eyes.
They knew they were all thinking the same thing.{p}

Everyone swallowed hard on the spit that had pooled in their mouths.
"...What happened?"
And they strained their ears toward where the voice had come from.
"Let's just go home!
Who cares about make-up class!"
Then one of the girls suddenly burst into tears.
The thread of tension she'd been holding taut must have snapped.
She wailed and wailed, so hard it was startling.
Without any care for how she looked.
"You're right, let's go home.
I think we should go home too.
It's the teacher's fault for leaving us here this late."
The other girl suggested it, rubbing the sobbing girl's back.
"Yeah. I think so too.
We should go home."
One of them chimed in, agreeing with her.
But there was someone who couldn't just go along with it.
"...But we can't just leave them, can we?
We heard a scream, at least.
Aren't we going to help them?"
It's true, it's hard to abandon your friends, isn't it?
The two who didn't come back were their classmates, after all.{p}

...Hey, {a}{f:|}.
Are we friends?{p}{f:Will you|If you'd like, will you} be my friend?
I'll be your friend
I won't be your friend

Thank you.
I'm so happy.
Ever since we first met, I've had a feeling you and I could be friends.
I'll never betray you.
Let's get along together from now on.
...That's right.
That's what friends are, isn't it?
Of course you can't abandon your friends.
It was the same for them, too.
But there was one guy who balked.{p}

"...That's easy for you to say.
That might be a sick joke, you know.
They're probably waiting somewhere along the way to jump out and scare us when we come to help.
So forget it, I'm telling you.
If anything, we should turn the tables and teach guys like that a painful lesson."
Even so, the one who'd first said they should go help him wouldn't back down.
"...Even if you guys don't come, I'm going.
If it's a joke, then at least we can stop worrying.
But if it isn't a joke...?
If something really did happen, what are you going to do then?"
"If you want to go, suit yourself.
I'm not going."
"Fine, I'll suit myself.
I'm going."{p}

Really, that's exactly when they should have stuck together.
But they got into a fight over something trivial.
And so only one of them, the brave one who cared about his friends, ended up going to the restroom.
Whatever the girls had said, when it came down to it, they were scared after all.
The remaining three decided to go to the faculty room to get the teacher.{p}Hey, {a}{f:|}.
Which of the two stories do you want me to continue?
The brave one who went to the restroom
The trio who headed for the faculty room

That's what I thought.
I was sure you'd want to hear that part of the story.
He went looking for a restroom, but there are three restrooms in all in the old school building.
This classroom we're in now is on the first floor, right?{p}Which floor's restroom do you think he went to?
The first-floor restroom
The second-floor restroom
The third-floor restroom

A world where only your own footsteps echo isn't a very pleasant place.
Had the other three gone to fetch a teacher for them by now?{p}
Worrying about other people like that, he tried to drive off the fear creeping up inside him.{p}
The voices seemed to be coming from the third floor.{p}

A twinge of regret brushed his heart: he should have gone to the faculty room with the other three.
But since he'd come all this way, he decided to turn the tables and scare them instead.{p}

With everything so dark around him, it was easy to focus on his hearing.
And from the voices he could hear mixed in with his own footsteps, he pinned down their position.
They were behind the wall at the top of the stairs leading to the third floor.
Having decided that, he braced himself as the third floor drew closer.
Then he stopped one step short of the top and took a deep breath.{p}

"Boo!"
And he shouted at the top of his lungs.
...But there was nobody there.
There wasn't even a shadow of the two who should have been there, and the voices he'd been hearing until then had stopped dead.
That was when the fear truly sank in all over again.
And he remembered.
The story of Hanako-san, who's said to appear in the third-floor restroom of the old school building.{p}

They say where Hanako-san is depends on her mood at the time.
Usually, she's supposed to be in the second stall from the back.
But sometimes she's in a different stall, so you can never feel safe.
Say you walk into the restroom.{p}
Then, even though the restroom should be empty, you hear a girl crying inside one of the stalls.{p}
So you knock three times, and three knocks come back from inside.{p}
Next, you knock just once.{p}
Then, once again, a single knock comes back.{p}
And then,

"Is anyone in there?"
you ask, but there's no answer.{p}
There's no answer, so, puzzled, you try to open the door, and it isn't locked.{p}
You work up your nerve and open the door, and there's nobody inside.{p}

So, thinking that's weird, you close the door, right?
Then, this time, someone knocks from the other side of the door.{p}

Through the gap above the stall door, a girl with a pale face and a bobbed haircut is staring straight down at you.
And the rumor goes that whoever she sees will die within three days.
That's the story of Hanako-san that haunts our school's old building.
And he went and remembered all of that.
But it's okay.
Hanako-san appears in the girls' restroom, after all.
She can't hurt him.
And he could hardly imagine the two who'd gone missing would be in the girls' restroom.{p}

When he came out on the third floor and glanced toward the restroom, the lights in the third-floor restroom weren't on.
In that case, which restroom on earth had they gone to...?{p}

And what had that scream been?
Suddenly, he grew scared of being alone.{p}

Telling himself there was nothing he could do alone anyway, he tried to run away.
That was when it happened.{p}

Suddenly, the lights in the third-floor restroom flashed on.
...Someone's there.
That's what he thought.
It had to be those two.
Those two had been trying to scare him after all.
They meant to frighten him again and again and push his terror to its peak.{p}
Once he thought that, he actually stopped being scared.{p}
He swore firmly to himself that he'd give those two what for, then puffed out his chest and walked toward the restroom.{p}
Ready to laugh right back at them whenever they tried to spook him.{p}

There was nobody in the restroom.
But all the stall doors were closed.
So they had to be in one of them.
There were four doors.
Which door do you think he opened first?{p}
The door farthest in the back
The second door from the back
The third door from the back
The door closest to the entrance

...There was nobody inside.
So, which one do you think he opened next?{p}

...There was nobody inside.
At last, it was the final door.{p}

He took hold of the knob of the remaining door.
What if they weren't in here...?
If this one was empty too, then who had turned on the restroom lights?
And where were they?
Nothing would add up anymore.
Thinking about it made his heart pound wildly.
To open it, or not to open it.
He agonized over it.
Still, he'd never get an answer unless he opened it.
He gripped the doorknob hard, if only to steady his trembling hand.{p}

And then he slowly turned the knob.
...That was when it happened.{p}

The screaming went on and on.
A male voice?
Or a female one?
An eerie shriek, as if not one person but many were screaming.
"It's coming from downstairs!"
The voices were coming from the floor below.
He practically flew down the stairs and looked down the long hallway.{p}

"Ah!"
He saw them.{p}
Far down the hallway, the three who were supposed to have gone to the faculty room, being dragged away.{p}
The three were still alive, screaming at the tops of their lungs for help.{p}

He couldn't understand why they were here, when they should have gone to the faculty room.
Had something attacked them on the way...?{p}

Something was dragging them, that much was certain, but he couldn't get a good look at it.
There seemed to be a number of small black lumps of some kind, and they were the ones dragging the three away.{p}
"Wait!"
He hurried after them.{p}

But in his rush, he slipped and fell.
And he hit his head hard.{p}

"Oww..."
He rubbed the back of his head, and froze in shock.
His head was slimy.
His hair was soaked and sticky.
Blood...?
He brought his slick fingers up to his nose.
It was definitely the smell of blood.
He rubbed his head again and realized there was no wound.{p}

So he looked down the dim hallway...
And there was blood smeared thick across the floor.
It ran on in one thick line, as if someone had run a paint roller down the hallway.
This was blood left by the three as they were dragged.
He knew it by instinct.{p}

He stood up and looked into the distance, and the three being dragged away were barely moving.
He couldn't hear them calling for help anymore.
Were they dead, or still just barely alive...?
The three were dragged all the way to the end of the hallway, and then around the corner.
And then they were gone from sight.{p}
Past that corner was another staircase.{p}

He hurried after them.
This time, taking care not to slip in the blood.{p}

Even around the corner, the trail where the three had been dragged was clearly visible.
Just like the trail a slug leaves behind.{p}

It led to the girls' restroom on the third floor.
What's more, the lights were on in the girls' restroom.
He caught his breath.
If he'd wanted to run, he could have.
But he didn't run.
Maybe he thought he'd become some hero on TV or something.
He slowly followed the trail of blood and stood in front of the girls' restroom.{p}

The restroom was hushed and still.
He had completely thrown out the idea that this was a prank set up by those two.
That they'd been hiding behind that last door he never opened after all, and now...
Because he knew full well himself how ridiculous an idea that was.{p}

The trail of blood went right on into the restroom.
Inside, the fluorescent lights were blazing brightly, you see.
It was strangely dazzling.
And on that floor, the blood was smeared thick.
Three lines had merged into one thick line.
The thin gaps here and there in the thick line were proof that it was three lines joined together.
That line led on, clear as anything.
To the second stall from the back, where Hanako-san is said to be.
There wasn't a single sound.
Besides, the stalls in the old building's restrooms are cramped.
No matter how you look at it, there's no way three people could fit in that space.
But judging by the trail of blood, they couldn't be anywhere else.{p}Hey, {a}{f:|}.
What do you think he did?{p}Do you think he opened the door of the stall where Hanako-san is said to be?
He opened it
He didn't open it

That's right.
As if lured in, he went and stood in front of that stall.{p}

And he put his hand on the knob.
The knob felt oddly heavy.{p}

But when he put some strength into it, the heaviness lasted only a moment, and the door opened easily.
And then...{p}

The door opened, but there was nothing inside.
The trail of blood that had run all the way from the second floor broke off abruptly inside that stall.
Even though it was empty inside.
Just then, he felt something cold on his cheek.
Rain...?
It couldn't possibly be raining.
This was inside the old school building.
Suspicious, he looked up...{p}

There they were.
The five classmates who'd been in the make-up class with him were stuck to the ceiling, covered in blood.
And clinging to one of them, a woman with a bobbed haircut, in a bloodstained sailor uniform, was glaring down at him.
He couldn't make out her face.{p}

Because she was wearing something like a white Noh mask, you see.
You couldn't even read her expression.
The five stuck to the ceiling had been nailed up through various parts of their bodies with five-inch spikes.
And the masked woman was clinging there, leaning her weight on their corpses.
He was struck speechless.
He couldn't even scream. He was transfixed by the eerie world that filled his vision.
That became his last memory.
Because the very next instant, the masked woman came skittering across the ceiling like a spider and was on him.
...And at that moment, he wondered.{p}
What were those small black creatures that had been carrying those three away...?{p}

It didn't matter one bit to him, since he was about to die.
Maybe people think about pretty silly things right before they die.{p}

...So what became of those six, you ask?
...They were never found.
The next day, the teacher who'd gone home and left them in the make-up class and the teacher who'd been asked to take over both searched the old school building before the problem could get any bigger.
But they didn't find their bodies, or even a single drop of blood.
And those two teachers got their stories straight: they said they'd sent the students home properly.
Awful, isn't it?
And so the six were listed as missing.
In the end, no one ever saw any of them again.
Still, their classmates knew the six who vanished had stayed behind at school for a make-up class.
And since they disappeared right after that, strange rumors started going around.{p}

All kinds of weird rumors spread, too: that strange groans could be heard from the girls' restroom on the third floor of the old school building, or that someone had seen the missing students there.
So people started saying it was Hanako-san's curse.
That Hanako-san had taken the six of them away.
Whether those six wandered into another world, or whether it really was Hanako-san's curse, nobody knows.
...And that's the end of the story about the old school building.
Of course, nobody actually saw the six of them being killed, so it isn't very credible, is it?{p}

But I just can't believe it was a lie.
...How about it?
Let's go to the girls' restroom on the third floor right now and try calling Hanako-san out.
{a}{f:|}.
You said earlier that you'd go, didn't you?
Or did hearing my story change your mind?{p}What'll it be?
You're coming, right?
Go to the third-floor girls' restroom
I'm not going after all

I'm so happy.
We really are friends.
No, I already think of you as my best friend.
You've got to solve the mystery of Hanako-san and write a great article.
Then I'll get to be proud, too.
...Even if I end up dead.
Well then, let's go.{p}

...{f:And that was when it happened|Just then}.
"{f:Whoa|Eek}!"
Just as {f:we|we} were about to get up from our seats, we were bathed in a blinding, intense light.
It was dazzling!
What {f:the hell is|is} this light?{p}{f:What the...|No}!
What {f:just happened|just happened}★{p}

We got up from our seats without a word.
When I happened to glance at the classroom clock, it read 10:20.
So was the story from before true after all?
At the very least, that clock had stopped.
Was there a skull-like stain on the back of it?
Maybe my eyes had gotten used to the dark, because I could get around well enough by moonlight alone.
...But if I'd known things would turn out like this, I would have brought a flashlight.
Hosoda and I left the classroom together.{p}
Even though it was summer, the wind felt awfully cold.{p}

Was that because I was scared?
This was the first floor.{p}

We climbed the stairs.
What a horrible sound they made.{p}

It sounded like vengeful spirits laughing at us.
We passed the second floor and kept on climbing the stairs to the third.{p}

Once we reached the top of the stairs and turned the corner, the girls' restroom would be on the left.
We turned the corner, and the girls' restroom we were heading for...{p}

Its light was on.
In the old school building, where no light should ever come on, and in the very girls' restroom where Hanako-san was said to be, the light was on.
"What do we do?
Should we go home after all?"
Hosoda whispered in my ear.
His voice was shrill and hoarse.
He wasn't even touching me, yet I could clearly feel his body trembling.
I couldn't stop myself from shaking, either.{p}

What should I do?
If I was going to turn back, now was the time.
And this was probably my last chance.
What should I do?
Keep going?
Or just go home?{p}
Go to the girls' restroom
Go home now

"Let's go."
When I said that, Hosoda took hold of my hand.
"...You're brave.
I'm scared.
I know it's strange for me to say this when I'm the one who suggested coming...
But I'm so scared I can't stand it."{p}

"Everyone who's told a story so far has disappeared.
Every time a story ends, something bad happens.
...It's my turn now, isn't it?
I'm the one who's going to disappear, aren't I?"{p}

Hosoda's hand was clammy with sweat.
And sweat was pouring from all over his face, glistening slickly.
"Please.
Please don't abandon me."
"I know."{p}
As I stepped forward, I could clearly feel Hosoda's hand tighten around mine.{p}

We stood in front of the girls' restroom.
"...We're going in."
Hosoda gave a small nod at my words.
There was nothing inside the restroom.
Maybe because it hadn't been used in a long time, an indescribable sour stench hung over everything.
...The second stall from the back.
